laws.title: Hashemite Constitutional Monarchy
laws.subtitle: Jordan's royal family holds executive authority
laws.fullDescription: Jordan is a constitutional monarchy ruled by the Hashemite dynasty. King Abdullah II has extensive constitutional powers including appointing and dismissing governments, dissolving parliament, and issuing royal decrees. The constitution was adopted in 1952 and has been amended multiple times. The king commands the armed forces and approves all legislation. While Jordan has an elected parliament, real power rests with the monarch. Jordan is considered a moderate Arab monarchy with relatively stable governance.
laws.penalty: N/A — constitutional framework
exceptions: Parliament can override royal decree in limited circumstances
Constitutional Court reviews legislation for conformity
laws.source: Constitution of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, 1952

quiz.q: What type of government does Jordan have?
options: Constitutional monarchy under the Hashemite dynasty
quiz.explanation: Jordan is a constitutional monarchy ruled by the Hashemite dynasty. King Abdullah II holds extensive constitutional powers and real executive authority, though there is an elected parliament.

laws.title: State Security Court
laws.subtitle: Special court for terrorism and political offenses
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's State Security Court (SSC) tries cases involving terrorism, espionage, drug trafficking above certain quantities, and offenses against the king. The court has been widely criticized by human rights organizations for procedural deficiencies including limited right to counsel during investigation, trials of civilians before military judges, and broad jurisdiction that sweeps in political dissidents and journalists. Jordan has used the SSC to prosecute individuals for social media posts critical of the government.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment to death depending on offense
exceptions: Regular courts handle most criminal matters
Constitutional Court has limited review authority over SSC
laws.source: Jordan State Security Court Law No. 17 of 1959 (amended)

quiz.q: What has the State Security Court been criticized for regarding political cases?
options: Procedural deficiencies including trials of civilians before military judges
quiz.explanation: Jordan's State Security Court has been criticized for procedural deficiencies including limited defense counsel access, trials of civilians before military judges, and broad jurisdiction used against journalists and social media users.

laws.title: Penal Code — Sexuality and Morality
laws.subtitle: Criminalization of same-sex conduct
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Penal Code does not explicitly criminalize same-sex sexual conduct, unlike many neighboring countries, but police use public decency provisions and public morality laws to arrest and detain LGBTQ+ persons. The situation for LGBTQ+ Jordanians is precarious — they face social stigma, family violence, and police harassment without explicit legal protection. Transgender persons have no legal recognition. Jordan is considered slightly more tolerant than some Gulf states but LGBTQ+ rights are severely limited.
laws.penalty: Fines and imprisonment under public decency laws; no specific homosexuality statute
exceptions: Private consensual conduct between adults rarely prosecuted under specific law
Some limited tolerance in Amman's urban areas in practice

quiz.q: How does Jordan's law differ from many neighboring countries regarding same-sex conduct?
options: Jordan has no law whatsoever on the subject
Jordan lacks an explicit criminalization statute but uses public morality laws
Jordan has the harshest penalties in the region
quiz.explanation: Unlike many neighboring countries, Jordan's Penal Code lacks an explicit statute criminalizing same-sex conduct, but police use public decency and morality provisions to arrest LGBTQ+ persons, and social stigma and family violence remain severe.

laws.title: Personal Status Law — Family Court
laws.subtitle: Islamic law governs marriage, divorce, and inheritance
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Personal Status Law governs marriage, divorce, custody, and inheritance for Muslims (approximately 97% of the population) according to Islamic law. The minimum marriage age was raised to 18 in 2019 with judicial exceptions. A husband can divorce by talaq (unilateral repudiation); a wife must go to court. Polygamy is permitted for up to four wives with court permission. Child custody defaults to mothers for young children then transfers to fathers. Christian personal status is governed by respective churches.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for child marriage without judicial exception
exceptions: Christian communities have their own personal status courts
2019 reform raised minimum age to 18 with judicial exceptions allowed
laws.source: Jordanian Personal Status Law No. 15 of 2019

quiz.q: What reform did Jordan make to its marriage laws in 2019?
options: Raised the minimum marriage age to 18 (with judicial exceptions)
Equalized divorce rights for men and women
Made marriage registration mandatory in all cases
quiz.explanation: Jordan's 2019 Personal Status Law raised the minimum marriage age to 18 for both sexes, though courts can grant exceptions, addressing decades of child marriage under the previous law which allowed marriage at younger ages.

laws.title: Cybercrime Law — Online Speech
laws.subtitle: Broad criminalization of online expression
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Cybercrime Law (2023) significantly expanded criminalization of online speech. The law has been widely criticized for its overly broad definitions that could criminalize satire, criticism of officials, and journalistic work. Journalists, bloggers, and social media users have been arrested for posts critical of the government, the king, or official policies. The law criminalizes 'spreading false news that harms national unity.' Jordan's press freedom ranking has deteriorated significantly.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment 3 months to 3 years; fines for most offenses
exceptions: News organizations with proper licensing may have some protection
Academic research with proper framing may be exempt

quiz.q: What broadly worded offense in Jordan's Cybercrime Law has been used against critics?
options: Spreading false news that harms national unity
quiz.explanation: Jordan's Cybercrime Law includes the broadly worded offense of 'spreading false news that harms national unity,' which has been used to arrest journalists, bloggers, and social media users for posts critical of government policy.

laws.title: Jordan's Aid-Dependent Economy
laws.subtitle: Foreign aid and remittances as economic pillars
laws.fullDescription: Jordan has few natural resources and relies heavily on foreign aid (particularly from the US and Gulf states) and remittances from Jordanians working abroad. The US-Jordan Free Trade Agreement (2000) was the first US FTA with an Arab country. The IMF has repeatedly supported Jordan through programs. Jordan's debt-to-GDP ratio is high. Water scarcity is an existential economic challenge — Jordan is the second most water-scarce country in the world. The large refugee population (Palestinian, Syrian, Iraqi) adds to economic pressures.
laws.penalty: N/A — economic policy framework
exceptions: Free trade zones offer investment incentives
Jordan's FTA with the US provides market access

quiz.q: What makes Jordan's water situation particularly severe?
options: Jordan is the second most water-scarce country in the world
quiz.explanation: Jordan is the second most water-scarce country in the world, with per-capita water availability far below the international water poverty line, making water security one of Jordan's most critical national challenges.

laws.title: Waqf and Islamic Institutions
laws.subtitle: Ministry of Awqaf manages Islamic endowments
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Ministry of Awqaf and Islamic Affairs manages religious endowments, mosques, and Islamic education. The ministry regulates Friday sermons to prevent extreme content. Jordan follows the Hanafi school of Islamic jurisprudence for most matters. The Supreme Islamic Council oversees Islamic courts. Jordan is home to some of Islam's holiest sites including the baptism site of Jesus (also significant in Islam) and parts of the biblical Holy Land. The Hashemite dynasty holds custodianship of Jerusalem's Islamic and Christian holy sites.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for misappropriation of waqf property
exceptions: Christian churches manage their own endowments
Government can manage waqf for public purposes in certain cases
laws.source: Jordanian Ministry of Awqaf and Islamic Affairs Law

quiz.q: What unique custodianship does Jordan's Hashemite dynasty hold regarding Jerusalem?
options: Custodianship of Islamic and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem
Legal authority over all religious sites in the Holy Land
quiz.explanation: Jordan's Hashemite dynasty holds the historic custodianship of Islamic and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem (particularly the Al-Aqsa Mosque and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre), a role maintained under the 1994 Wadi Araba peace treaty with Israel.

laws.title: Electoral System — Tribal and Quota Politics
laws.subtitle: Elections with tribal, women's, and minority quotas
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's electoral system has historically favored tribal, rural, and East Bank Jordanian communities over Palestinians and urban populations. The one-person-one-vote system and gerrymandered districts have been criticized for preventing genuine political competition. Quota seats are reserved for women (15%), Christians (9 seats), Circassians/Chechens (3 seats), and Bedouin tribes. Jordan has never allowed genuine political parties to contest power — tribal loyalties dominate. The Muslim Brotherhood's Islamic Action Front has periodically boycotted elections.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for electoral fraud
exceptions: Quota system ensures minimum representation for minorities
Palestinian-majority cities are structurally underrepresented

quiz.q: What percentage of Jordan's parliamentary seats are reserved for women through quota?
quiz.explanation: Jordan's Electoral Law reserves 15% of parliamentary seats for women through a quota system, ensuring minimum representation. Jordan also has reserved seats for Christians, Circassians/Chechens, and Bedouin tribes.

laws.title: Lèse-Majesté — Insulting the King
laws.subtitle: Criticism of the king is a criminal offense
laws.fullDescription: Insulting or defaming the king is a criminal offense in Jordan under the Penal Code. The Press and Publications Law and Cybercrime Law extend similar protections to members of the royal family and senior officials. Several journalists have been prosecuted for social media posts deemed disrespectful to the monarchy. Jordan uses these laws to limit criticism of the royal family and government policies attributed to the king. The State Security Court handles most such cases.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment 1-3 years for insulting the king; additional penalties for publication
exceptions: Constructive criticism of government policy is theoretically permitted
Academic and historical discussion of the monarchy differs from insult

quiz.q: Under which court are insult-of-king cases typically tried in Jordan?
quiz.explanation: Cases involving insulting the king are typically tried before Jordan's State Security Court, which handles national security and politically sensitive offenses, often with reduced procedural protections compared to regular courts.

laws.title: Palestinian Refugee Status
laws.subtitle: Jordan's large Palestinian refugee population
laws.fullDescription: Jordan hosts the world's largest Palestinian refugee population — over 2.2 million registered with UNRWA plus many more unregistered. Palestinians in Jordan have varying legal statuses: most East Bank Palestinians have Jordanian citizenship; Gaza Palestinians may have limited or temporary documentation; West Bank Palestinians may hold Jordanian passports without full citizenship. The Palestinian refugee issue is central to Jordan's politics, economy, and identity. Jordan's 1994 peace treaty with Israel is linked to the Palestinian refugee question.
laws.penalty: N/A — refugee legal status issue
exceptions: Gaza Palestinians in Jordan have had their status periodically reviewed
Stateless Palestinians have limited rights and no travel documents
laws.source: UNRWA Jordan Registration Data; Jordanian Nationality Law

quiz.q: How many Palestinians are registered with UNRWA in Jordan?
quiz.explanation: Jordan hosts over 2.2 million Palestinians registered with UNRWA, making it the largest Palestinian refugee population in the world, plus many additional Palestinians who are unregistered or have Jordanian citizenship.

laws.title: Anti-Terrorism Law
laws.subtitle: Broad counter-terrorism legislation
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Anti-Terrorism Law (2006, amended 2014) contains broad definitions of terrorism that include acts intended to 'disrupt public order' or 'harm national unity.' Human rights organizations have documented the law's use against peaceful protesters, journalists, labor activists, and members of opposition groups. The State Security Court handles terrorism cases. Jordan faces genuine terrorism threats from ISIS and other groups, but the law's broad scope has been used as a tool for political repression.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment 5-15 years for most terrorism offenses; death penalty for attacks causing death
exceptions: Legitimate political activity technically not covered
Security cooperation with Western countries has influenced some enforcement priorities

quiz.q: What activities beyond genuine terrorism have been prosecuted under Jordan's Anti-Terrorism Law?
options: Peaceful protesters, journalists, and opposition members
quiz.explanation: Jordan's Anti-Terrorism Law has been used against peaceful protesters, journalists, labor activists, and opposition members due to its broad definitions that include acts intended to 'disrupt public order' or 'harm national unity.'

laws.title: Syrian Refugee Work Permits
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for Syrian refugee employment
laws.fullDescription: Jordan hosts approximately 670,000 registered Syrian refugees (and potentially twice as many unregistered). The Jordan Compact (2016) established a framework allowing Syrian refugees to access formal employment in exchange for preferential EU trade access for Jordanian goods from special economic zones. Refugees have been legally permitted to work in certain sectors. However, barriers including work permit costs, employer reluctance, and sectoral restrictions have limited formal employment uptake. Most Syrians work informally.
laws.penalty: Fines for employers hiring refugees without work permits
exceptions: Special Economic Zones have expanded refugee employment
Humanitarian workers authorized to work without standard permits
laws.source: Jordan Compact 2016; Labour Law amendments for refugees

quiz.q: What was the Jordan Compact of 2016?
options: A military alliance with Western countries
An agreement allowing Syrian refugees to access formal employment in exchange for preferential EU trade access
An economic aid package from Gulf states
quiz.explanation: The Jordan Compact (2016) established a framework allowing Syrian refugees to access formal employment in Jordan in exchange for preferential trade access to EU markets for Jordanian goods produced in special economic zones.

laws.title: Water Scarcity Crisis
laws.subtitle: Jordan's existential water security challenge
laws.fullDescription: Jordan receives an average of just 111mm of rainfall annually and has per-capita water availability far below the water poverty line. The Jordan River — central to the region's religious and cultural heritage — has been reduced to a trickle by Israeli and Jordanian water diversions. Non-renewable fossil aquifers are being depleted at unsustainable rates. The Disi Aquifer water convoy project brings water from southern Jordan. Jordan receives significant volumes of treated wastewater for agricultural use. Climate change threatens to further reduce rainfall.
laws.penalty: Fines for unauthorized water use and water theft
exceptions: Agricultural water use has different licensing under complex water law
Emergency water allocation during drought overrides normal allocation
laws.source: Jordanian Water Authority Law; National Water Strategy

quiz.q: What has happened to the Jordan River due to water diversions?
options: It has been reduced to a trickle
It has been redirected entirely to Israel
quiz.explanation: The Jordan River — of profound religious significance and once a substantial waterway — has been reduced to a trickle by water diversions by Israel, Jordan, and Syria, carrying only about 2% of its historic flow and facing severe ecological degradation.

laws.title: Housing Law — Urban Development
laws.subtitle: Property ownership and urban planning
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Land Registration Department manages property registration. The Law on Ownership of Real Estate by Non-Jordanians governs foreign property ownership, which requires approval and is restricted in some areas. Amman has experienced rapid urbanization. Palestinian refugees' access to property ownership has historically been restricted. Housing affordability is a significant challenge for young Jordanians. Informal settlements (particularly around Amman) house significant populations without legal title.
laws.penalty: Fines for illegal construction; squatters can be evicted
exceptions: Palestinian refugees in some camps have limited property rights under UNRWA framework
Heritage buildings have special protection against demolition
laws.source: Jordanian Land Registration Law; Urban Development Regulations

quiz.q: What challenge does housing represent for young Jordanians?
options: Too many housing options creating confusion
Affordability — high housing costs relative to incomes
quiz.explanation: Housing affordability is a significant challenge for young Jordanians, with high housing costs relative to local incomes making homeownership difficult for many young families and contributing to urban informal settlement growth.

laws.title: Drug Laws
laws.subtitle: Strict narcotics penalties
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Law imposes strict penalties for drug trafficking and possession. Jordan is a transit country for drugs moving through the Middle East (particularly captagon from Syria through Jordan to Gulf markets). Drug trafficking by criminal networks linked to regime-adjacent figures in Syria has been documented. The Anti-Narcotics Department enforces drug laws. Captagon — a amphetamine-type stimulant — has become a particularly significant challenge given production in Syria.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment 1-10 years for possession; death penalty for trafficking involving serious offenses
exceptions: Prescription medications with controlled substances regulated separately
First-time offenders may receive treatment referrals
laws.source: Jordan Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Law No. 11 of 1988

quiz.q: What drug has become particularly challenging for Jordan given its production in Syria?
quiz.explanation: Captagon — an amphetamine-type stimulant — produced primarily in Syria and transiting through Jordan to Gulf markets has become a significant drug enforcement challenge, with production linked to regime-adjacent networks in Syria.

laws.title: Dead Sea — Environmental Crisis
laws.subtitle: The Dead Sea is shrinking rapidly
laws.fullDescription: The Dead Sea, bordering Jordan, Israel, and the Palestinian territories, is shrinking at an alarming rate — losing over 1 meter of water level annually. The main cause is diversion of water from the Jordan River (which feeds the Dead Sea) for agriculture and domestic use. Sinkholes are forming along the Israeli and Jordanian shorelines as salt dissolves underground. A proposed Red Sea-Dead Sea Canal (RSDSC) project to replenish the Dead Sea from the Gulf of Aqaba has been discussed for decades but remains unfunded.
laws.penalty: Fines for unauthorized mining of Dead Sea minerals
exceptions: Dead Sea minerals mined by authorized companies (Arab Potash Company in Jordan, ICL in Israel)
Research and scientific access permitted under special permits
laws.source: Jordan Rift Valley development plans; RSDSC Environmental Assessment

quiz.q: At what rate is the Dead Sea losing water level?
quiz.explanation: The Dead Sea is losing over 1 meter of water level annually due primarily to diversion of water from the Jordan River for agriculture and domestic use, creating a severe environmental crisis affecting both the Jordanian and Israeli shorelines.

laws.title: Intelligence Services — GID
laws.subtitle: General Intelligence Directorate's extensive powers
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's General Intelligence Directorate (GID, known locally as the mukhabarat) is a powerful security agency with a reputation for pervasive surveillance of Jordanian society. The GID monitors political opposition, civil society organizations, and media. It operates Jwaideh Prison and other detention facilities. The GID has been implicated in torture and ill-treatment of detainees. Despite reforms, the GID maintains significant influence over Jordanian political life. The GID has cooperated with Western intelligence agencies in counter-terrorism.
laws.penalty: N/A — security service; detainees have limited legal recourse
exceptions: GID operations are classified and not subject to normal judicial oversight
International intelligence cooperation has provided some accountability pressure
laws.source: Jordanian Intelligence Law; Human Rights Watch documentation

quiz.q: What is the colloquial term used for Jordan's General Intelligence Directorate?
quiz.explanation: The GID (General Intelligence Directorate) is colloquially known as the 'mukhabarat' in Jordan, a term for intelligence/secret police services widely used across the Arab world, and is known for pervasive surveillance of Jordanian society.

laws.title: Judicial System — Independence
laws.subtitle: Courts with limited independence from executive
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's judicial system includes civil, religious, and special courts. The Judicial Council oversees judicial appointments. Jordan's courts are generally considered more independent than many regional peers, but executive influence remains significant, particularly in politically sensitive cases. The Constitutional Court was established in 2012. Jordan has a functioning Court of Cassation (Supreme Court). The rule of law is generally upheld in commercial matters, but national security cases fall to the more politicized State Security Court.
laws.penalty: N/A — judicial structure
exceptions: Commercial courts operate with considerable independence
Religious courts apply Islamic law for personal status matters
laws.source: Jordanian Judicial Council Law; Constitutional Court Law 2012

quiz.q: When was Jordan's Constitutional Court established?
quiz.explanation: Jordan established its Constitutional Court in 2012, providing formal judicial review of legislation for constitutional conformity — a relatively recent addition to Jordan's judicial architecture that operates alongside the regular court system.

laws.title: Aqaba Special Economic Zone
laws.subtitle: Free trade zone at the Red Sea port
laws.fullDescription: The Aqaba Special Economic Zone (ASEZA) was established in 2000 to transform Aqaba into a business and tourism hub. ASEZA has its own authority and regulatory framework separate from Jordanian law in many respects. Jordan's only seaport (Aqaba Port) is critical for trade. ASEZA has attracted investment in tourism, industry, and logistics. The zone has streamlined business registration, tax incentives, and simplified labor regulations to attract foreign investment.
laws.penalty: ASEZA-specific penalties for zone regulation violations
exceptions: ASEZA businesses have special tax treatment including 5% flat tax
Special labor rules apply in ASEZA zone
laws.source: Aqaba Special Economic Zone Authority Law No. 32 of 2000

quiz.q: What is significant about Aqaba's port for Jordan?
options: It is Jordan's largest river port
It is Jordan's only seaport, making it critical for all sea trade
It is jointly operated with Israel
It is the largest port in the Middle East
quiz.explanation: Aqaba Port is Jordan's only seaport, making it the exclusive gateway for Jordan's maritime trade — a critical chokepoint for the economy of this landlocked country that depends heavily on imports.

laws.title: Public Assemblies Law
laws.subtitle: Restrictions on protests and assembly
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Public Assemblies Law requires prior notification (effectively permission) for public demonstrations. Security forces have dispersed protests using tear gas and arrests. The Arab Spring (2011-2012) prompted significant protests in Jordan that led to some constitutional reforms, but the government also tightened restrictions on public gatherings. Labor unions and professional associations have organized protests on economic issues. Protests related to Palestinian solidarity have been permitted at times and restricted at others.
laws.penalty: Criminal charges for unauthorized assembly; police can disperse protests
exceptions: Approved demonstrations by registered political parties and unions
Religious gatherings generally permitted
laws.source: Jordan Public Assemblies Law No. 7 of 2004

quiz.q: What did the 2011-2012 Arab Spring protests in Jordan lead to?
options: Some constitutional reforms while assembly restrictions were also tightened
quiz.explanation: Jordan's Arab Spring protests (2011-2012) led to some constitutional reforms including establishment of the Constitutional Court, but the government also used the period to tighten restrictions on public assemblies and political opposition.

laws.title: Labour Code — Worker Protections
laws.subtitle: Formal sector employment standards
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Labour Law establishes rights for formal sector workers including maximum working hours (8/day, 48/week), minimum leave, and anti-discrimination protections. Jordan has set a national minimum wage. Trade unions are permitted but their rights are restricted — strikes require lengthy procedural steps and are often blocked. Jordan has a significant migrant worker population (in construction, domestic work, and agriculture) who face additional vulnerabilities. The kafala (sponsorship) system for migrant workers gives employers excessive power.
laws.penalty: Fines for Labour Law violations; employment dispute boards handle claims
exceptions: Domestic workers are excluded from many Labour Law protections
Agricultural workers have different provisions

quiz.q: What system gives Jordanian employers excessive control over migrant workers?
quiz.explanation: The kafala (sponsorship) system ties migrant workers' legal status in Jordan to their employer, giving employers excessive power over workers who cannot change jobs or leave the country without employer permission.

laws.title: Education System — UNRWA and National Schools
laws.subtitle: Dual education system for refugees and citizens
laws.fullDescription: Jordan operates a dual education system: the national Ministry of Education system for Jordanian citizens, and the UNRWA school system for Palestinian refugees. UNRWA operates over 170 schools in Jordan serving approximately 120,000 Palestinian refugee students. Jordan's public education quality is considered reasonable by regional standards. The KHCC (King Hussein Cancer Center) and Royal Scientific Society represent Jordan's science and health education investment. Youth unemployment despite education credentials is a significant social challenge.
laws.penalty: N/A — educational policy
exceptions: Private schools serve wealthier families outside both systems
Syrian refugees have been incorporated into government schools via double-shift system
laws.source: Jordan Ministry of Education; UNRWA Jordan Education Program

quiz.q: How does Jordan accommodate Syrian refugee students in its education system?
options: Via double-shift system in government schools
quiz.explanation: Jordan accommodates Syrian refugee students primarily through a double-shift system in government schools — Jordanian students attend in the morning shift and Syrian refugee students in the afternoon shift, under significant pressure on infrastructure.

laws.title: Dana Biosphere Reserve — Conservation
laws.subtitle: Biodiversity protection in Jordan's natural reserves
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Dana Biosphere Reserve is one of the Middle East's most important nature reserves, protecting a unique mix of Mediterranean, steppe, and desert ecosystems. The Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature (RSCN) manages Jordan's protected areas network. Wadi Rum (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) is one of the world's most spectacular desert landscapes. Jordan has relatively progressive conservation legislation for the region. The Black Iris — Jordan's national flower — is protected under wildlife law.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for hunting protected species or damaging conservation areas
exceptions: Traditional Bedouin access to some areas may be accommodated
Scientific research with RSCN permits permitted
laws.source: Jordanian Environment Protection Law; RSCN Conservation Areas

quiz.q: What UNESCO World Heritage Site in Jordan is famous for its spectacular desert landscape?
quiz.explanation: Wadi Rum, a vast desert valley in southern Jordan, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its spectacular sandstone cliffs and desert landscapes, featured in films including Lawrence of Arabia and The Martian.

laws.title: Honour Crimes — Legal Reform
laws.subtitle: Gradual legislative reform on honour-based violence
laws.fullDescription: Jordan has a history of so-called 'honour crimes' where family members kill women suspected of sexual misconduct. The former Penal Code Article 98 (reduced sentences for crimes committed in 'fit of fury') was widely used to reduce sentences for honour killings. After years of advocacy, Jordan amended the law in 2017 and again in 2022 to eliminate this mitigation, making full prison sentences mandatory for honour killings. Women's rights organizations continue to document cases and advocate for full implementation.
laws.penalty: Life imprisonment for murder now mandatory; reduced mitigation clauses eliminated in 2017 and 2022
exceptions: Victim family members can grant pardons that reduce sentences
Full implementation and cultural change remains ongoing challenge

quiz.q: What legal change did Jordan make regarding honour killings in 2017 and 2022?
options: Introduced the first criminal penalties for honour killings
Eliminated the reduced sentence mitigation clause, making full prison sentences mandatory
Decriminalized honour killings for family members
Only changed the name of the offense
quiz.explanation: Jordan eliminated the reduced sentence mitigation clause (formerly Article 98 'fit of fury' defense) for honour killings in 2017 and strengthened this in 2022, making full life imprisonment mandatory — a significant but still-evolving legal reform.

laws.title: Amman Stock Exchange
laws.subtitle: Capital markets in Jordan
laws.fullDescription: The Amman Stock Exchange (ASE) was established in 1999 as a privatized, self-regulatory organization. The Jordan Securities Commission oversees market regulation. The ASE lists over 180 companies and is one of the Arab world's more developed stock exchanges. Major listed companies include Arab Bank (one of the Arab world's largest banks), Jordan Telecom (Orange Jordan), and potash producers. Foreign investment in Jordanian securities is permitted with some restrictions. The exchange has faced challenges from regional instability affecting investor confidence.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for insider trading and market manipulation
exceptions: Government bond market operates under different rules
Some state-related entities have special listing requirements

quiz.q: When was the Amman Stock Exchange established?
quiz.explanation: The Amman Stock Exchange was established in 1999 as a privatized, self-regulatory organization, replacing the earlier Amman Financial Market, and has developed into one of the Arab world's more developed capital markets.

laws.title: Jordan-Israel Peace Treaty — Wadi Araba
laws.subtitle: 1994 peace agreement with significant legal implications
laws.fullDescription: Jordan signed the Wadi Araba Peace Treaty with Israel in 1994, the second Arab state to do so after Egypt (1979). The treaty normalized relations, resolved border disputes, addressed water sharing, and committed to cooperation on economic and security issues. Jordan's custodianship of Jerusalem's holy sites was acknowledged. Public opinion in Jordan has remained resistant to normalization — popular sentiment is significantly more hostile to Israel than official policy. The treaty has been maintained through successive Israeli governments.
laws.penalty: N/A — international treaty
exceptions: Jordan has recalled its ambassador during Israeli military operations in Gaza
Some border and water provisions renegotiated over time

quiz.q: When did Jordan sign the Wadi Araba Peace Treaty with Israel?
quiz.explanation: Jordan signed the Wadi Araba Peace Treaty with Israel in 1994, becoming the second Arab state to normalize relations with Israel after Egypt's 1979 Camp David peace treaty, resolving border disputes and establishing cooperation frameworks.

laws.title: Migrant Domestic Workers
laws.subtitle: Domestic workers largely excluded from labor law
laws.fullDescription: Jordan has approximately 100,000+ migrant domestic workers, primarily from the Philippines, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and Ethiopia. Domestic workers are largely excluded from the Labour Law's protections. They work under the kafala (sponsorship) system and face significant risks of exploitation, abuse, and wage theft. Many domestic workers have sought refuge in their countries' embassies to escape abusive employers. Jordan has implemented a Unified Contract for domestic workers but enforcement is weak.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for employer abuse exist but are rarely enforced
exceptions: Jordanian law technically prohibits torture and cruel treatment
Embassies of sending countries can provide some protection
laws.source: Jordan Labour Law (domestic worker exclusions); Unified Contract for Domestic Workers

quiz.q: Under what system do migrant domestic workers in Jordan work, giving employers excessive control?
quiz.explanation: Migrant domestic workers in Jordan work under the kafala (sponsorship) system, which ties their legal status to their employer, creating significant power imbalances that have led to documented cases of exploitation, abuse, and wage theft.

laws.title: Muslim Brotherhood — Legal Status
laws.subtitle: Islamic Action Front and the Muslim Brotherhood in Jordan
laws.fullDescription: The Muslim Brotherhood operates legally in Jordan through the Islamic Action Front (IAF) political party, although the government has tried to limit its influence. Jordan licensed a new Brotherhood society in 2015 that it considers the 'official' Muslim Brotherhood, in competition with the historic Brotherhood. The IAF has boycotted multiple elections over the electoral system, re-entering in 2024. The Brotherhood's relative tolerance in Jordan (unlike Egypt or the UAE) reflects Jordan's balancing act between Islamist sentiment and regime security.
laws.penalty: Members of unlicensed Brotherhood organizations face prosecution
exceptions: IAF as political party operates legally within electoral framework
Religious and charitable activities separately regulated
laws.source: Jordanian Political Parties Law; Public Security Law

quiz.q: How does Jordan's approach to the Muslim Brotherhood differ from Egypt and the UAE?
options: Jordan has banned it more strictly
Jordan allows it to operate through the Islamic Action Front political party
Jordan has no restrictions at all
Jordan requires Brotherhood to be a government ministry
quiz.explanation: Unlike Egypt and the UAE which have banned the Muslim Brotherhood as a terrorist organization, Jordan allows it to operate through the Islamic Action Front (IAF) political party, reflecting a balancing act between Islamist sentiment and regime security.

laws.title: Renewable Energy — Solar Leadership
laws.subtitle: Jordan's solar energy transition
laws.fullDescription: Jordan has become a regional leader in solar energy development, with significant solar farm capacity installed at Ma'an and other sites. The energy sector was opened to independent power producers. Jordan imports 96% of its energy needs (mainly natural gas from Egypt and Iraq), making energy security a critical issue. Renewable energy targets aim to reach 50% renewable electricity by 2030. The Mafraq solar park and other projects have attracted international investment. Jordan has limited oil and gas resources but significant solar and wind potential.
laws.penalty: Energy regulation violations subject to fines
exceptions: Small household solar installations have simplified permitting
Off-grid systems in rural areas encouraged
laws.source: Jordan Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Law No. 13 of 2012

quiz.q: What percentage of its energy needs does Jordan currently import?
quiz.explanation: Jordan imports approximately 96% of its energy needs, primarily natural gas from Egypt and Iraq, making energy security one of Jordan's most critical national vulnerabilities and driving its significant investment in renewable energy.

laws.title: Family Reunification — Nationality Law
laws.subtitle: Discriminatory nationality transmission rules
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Nationality Law does not allow Jordanian women to transmit citizenship to their children or foreign husbands. Children of Jordanian mothers and foreign fathers cannot claim Jordanian citizenship — only children of Jordanian fathers are automatically citizens. This discriminatory provision has left many children of Jordanian women married to Palestinian, Iraqi, or other men stateless or with uncertain status. Women's rights organizations have campaigned for equal nationality rights. The UN Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination Against Women has repeatedly criticized this provision.
laws.penalty: Administrative consequences — lack of citizenship affects access to education, healthcare, and employment
exceptions: Children can apply for documentation of some services without full citizenship

laws.fullDescription: Jordan's disability rights law, enacted in 2017, aligns with the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities which Jordan ratified in 2008. The law establishes the Higher Council for the Affairs of Persons with Disabilities as the primary oversight body. It mandates accessibility in public buildings, transportation, and services, and prohibits employment discrimination. Implementation has been uneven — accessibility in public spaces remains poor outside major urban centers. Disability rights organizations have called for stronger enforcement mechanisms.
laws.penalty: Fines for discrimination; government buildings must comply with accessibility standards
exceptions: Heritage and historic buildings may be exempt from full accessibility requirements
Small businesses below a certain size have longer compliance timelines
Emergency measures may temporarily limit accessibility accommodations

quiz.q: When did Jordan ratify the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities?
quiz.explanation: Jordan ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2008, with the domestic disability rights law enacted in 2017.

laws.title: Trademark and Patent Law — Industrial Property Protection
laws.subtitle: Jordan's IP framework and TRIPS compliance
laws.fullDescription: Jordan enacted comprehensive intellectual property legislation as a condition of its WTO accession in 2000. The Industrial Property Law covers trademarks, patents, and industrial designs. Patent protection lasts 20 years; trademark protection is renewable indefinitely. Pharmaceutical patents have been a particularly contentious area given Jordan's large generic drugs industry and public health needs. Jordan faces pressure from US industry groups over pharmaceutical IP enforcement. The IP system is administered through the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply's IP Directorate.
laws.penalty: Fines and imprisonment for infringement; customs seizure of counterfeit goods
exceptions: Compulsory licensing permitted for public health emergencies under TRIPS flexibilities
Government use of patents for non-commercial purposes permitted
Parallel imports allowed under certain conditions

quiz.q: Jordan enacted IP legislation as a condition of accession to which organization?
quiz.explanation: Jordan enacted comprehensive intellectual property legislation as a condition of its WTO accession in 2000, covering trademarks, patents, and industrial designs.

laws.title: General Intelligence Directorate (GID) — Powers and Oversight
laws.subtitle: Jordan's domestic intelligence agency and its legal framework
laws.fullDescription: The General Intelligence Directorate (Mukhabarat) is Jordan's primary domestic and foreign intelligence service, operating under the direct authority of the king. Its legal framework is classified in significant parts. The GID has broad powers to detain suspected threats to national security, sometimes for extended periods without charge. It operates separately from the regular police and its detainees are typically held in different facilities. Human rights organizations have documented torture and ill-treatment in GID custody. The GID plays a central role in monitoring political dissidents, Islamist movements, and foreign intelligence threats.
laws.penalty: N/A — operates outside normal criminal law framework; detainees can be held without charge
exceptions: Formal criminal charges must eventually be filed or detainees released
The State Security Court provides nominal judicial oversight
International pressure has led to some reforms in acknowledged cases

quiz.q: Under whose direct authority does Jordan's General Intelligence Directorate (GID) operate?
quiz.explanation: Jordan's General Intelligence Directorate (Mukhabarat) operates under the direct authority of the king, giving it a special status outside normal governmental accountability structures.

laws.title: Agricultural Land Law — Use Restrictions and Preservation
laws.subtitle: Regulates agricultural land conversion and use in Jordan
laws.fullDescription: Jordan strictly regulates the conversion of agricultural land to non-agricultural uses given food security concerns and limited arable land — only 3% of Jordan's territory is arable. The Agricultural Land Law requires Ministry of Agriculture approval for rezoning. Violations including unauthorized construction on agricultural land are subject to demolition orders. The Jordan Valley, which contains the most productive agricultural land, is subject to special development authority governance. Land reform efforts have attempted to modernize farming practices and encourage consolidation of fragmented landholdings.
laws.penalty: Demolition orders for unauthorized construction; fines; revocation of agricultural subsidies
exceptions: Development corridors for infrastructure may override agricultural protections
Special Economic Zones can supersede standard land use restrictions
Military installations exempt from civilian land use regulations

quiz.q: What percentage of Jordan's territory is classified as arable land?
quiz.explanation: Only approximately 3% of Jordan's territory is arable land, making agricultural land preservation a major policy priority.

laws.title: Minimum Wage Law and Wage Council
laws.subtitle: Jordan's minimum wage framework and adjustment process
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's minimum wage is set by the Wages Council, a tripartite body of government, employer, and worker representatives. As of 2023, the minimum wage was JD 260 per month (approximately USD 367). The minimum wage applies to Jordanian workers and legally resident foreign workers, though enforcement for migrants is weaker in practice. Domestic workers are excluded from the statutory minimum wage. Jordan's National Aid Fund provides social assistance to families below the poverty line. The minimum wage is periodically revised, with increases negotiated against inflation and economic conditions.
laws.penalty: Fines for employers paying below minimum wage; Labour Ministry enforcement
exceptions: Domestic workers excluded from minimum wage provisions
Apprentices and trainees may receive below minimum wage
Agricultural workers subject to different standards in some governorates

quiz.q: Which body sets Jordan's minimum wage?
quiz.explanation: Jordan's minimum wage is set by the Wages Council, a tripartite body representing government, employers, and workers.

laws.title: Controlled Substances and Pharmaceutical Law
laws.subtitle: Regulates pharmaceutical manufacturing, import, and prescription
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's pharmaceutical sector is one of the most developed in the Arab world, with over 20 major manufacturing companies exporting to regional and global markets. The Jordan Food and Drug Administration (JFDA) regulates drug approval, manufacturing standards, and distribution. Counterfeit medicines are subject to significant penalties. Prescription requirements are enforced for controlled substances but informally relaxed for common medications. Jordan is a significant generic drug manufacturer and has navigated tensions between intellectual property obligations and affordable access to medicines.
laws.penalty: Fines and imprisonment for pharmaceutical fraud, counterfeiting, and unauthorized import
exceptions: Parallel imports of approved medicines permitted in some circumstances
Humanitarian exemptions for emergency medical supplies
Generic equivalents to off-patent medicines freely produced

quiz.q: Which Jordanian body is responsible for pharmaceutical regulation and drug approval?
quiz.explanation: The Jordan Food and Drug Administration (JFDA) regulates drug approval, manufacturing standards, and distribution in Jordan.

laws.title: Senate (Majlis al-Ayan) — Royal Appointment Powers
laws.subtitle: Jordan's appointed upper house and its constitutional role
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's parliament is bicameral: the elected House of Representatives (Majlis al-Nuwaab) and the appointed Senate (Majlis al-Ayan). The 65-seat Senate is entirely appointed by the king, typically from former senior officials, military officers, and tribal leaders. The Senate must approve all legislation passed by the lower house and can delay or reject bills. In practice, the Senate rarely blocks royal-backed legislation. This structure ensures elite loyalty while maintaining a democratic facade. The 2011 reforms did not alter Senate appointment powers.
laws.penalty: N/A — constitutional structure
exceptions: Budget bills can be overridden by joint parliament session if Senate delays
Constitutional amendments require two-thirds approval from both chambers
Emergency legislation can be passed by Royal Decree when parliament is in recess

quiz.q: How are members of Jordan's Senate (Majlis al-Ayan) selected?
quiz.explanation: All 65 members of Jordan's Senate are appointed by the king, typically from former senior officials, military officers, and tribal leaders.

laws.title: Copyright Law No. 22 of 1992 (Amended 1999)
laws.subtitle: Governs copyright protection for creative and intellectual works
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Copyright Law protects literary, artistic, and scientific works including software. Protection lasts 50 years after the author's death for most works. The law has been criticized for inadequate protection of foreign works, but amendments brought it closer to international standards following WTO accession. Piracy of software, music, and films remains prevalent. The Ministry of Culture administers copyright registration, though registration is not required for protection. The law covers both moral rights (attribution) and economic rights (reproduction, distribution).
laws.penalty: Fines and imprisonment for copyright infringement; seizure of infringing goods
exceptions: Educational use with attribution may qualify as fair use
Quotation for criticism and commentary permitted
Government documents not subject to copyright protection

quiz.q: How long does copyright protection last in Jordan after the author's death?
quiz.explanation: Jordan's Copyright Law protects works for 50 years after the author's death, in line with minimum international standards.

laws.title: Industrial Development Law and Special Economic Zones
laws.subtitle: Jordan's industrial zones and development area incentives
laws.fullDescription: Jordan operates multiple industrial zones and development areas offering tax incentives to attract investment. The Aqaba Special Economic Zone (ASEZ) offers near-zero taxes and customs duties for businesses operating in the port city. The Jordan Industrial Estates Corporation manages industrial estates in Zarqa, Irbid, and other cities. Investment in development zones — designated less-developed governorates — receives additional incentives. Despite these frameworks, unemployment remains high, particularly youth unemployment exceeding 40% in some measurements.
laws.penalty: N/A — incentive framework; tax fraud subject to standard penalties
exceptions: ASEZ has its own regulatory framework distinct from mainland Jordan

Defense-related industries subject to separate oversight

Near-zero taxes and customs duties for operating businesses
It is managed by the World Bank
quiz.explanation: Jordan's Aqaba Special Economic Zone (ASEZ) offers near-zero taxes and customs duties for businesses, making it a key investment attraction tool.

laws.title: Gender-Based Violence Law — Gaps and Reform Efforts
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for addressing domestic and gender-based violence
laws.fullDescription: Jordan lacks a comprehensive standalone law specifically addressing domestic violence. The Penal Code provides general protections against assault, but specific provisions for domestic violence are weak. The Family Protection Law of 2008 established Family Protection Departments within police stations to handle domestic violence cases. A draft Protection from Domestic Violence Law has been debated for years but not enacted as of 2024. Honour crime provisions in Article 340 of the Penal Code were reformed in 2017 to eliminate explicit mitigation for honour crimes, though full enforcement remains challenged.
laws.penalty: General assault provisions apply; enhanced penalties for repeated domestic violence through existing code

options: Honour crimes were fully criminalized with mandatory minimum sentences
Article 340 was reformed to eliminate explicit mitigation for honour killings
A separate tribunal was created for honour crime cases
quiz.explanation: In 2017, Jordan reformed Article 340 of the Penal Code to eliminate the explicit legal mitigation that had previously reduced sentences for honour killings.

laws.title: Traffic Law and Road Safety Legislation
laws.subtitle: Jordan's traffic regulations and enforcement
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Traffic Law sets speed limits, licensing requirements, vehicle inspection standards, and penalties for violations. Driving while intoxicated is illegal — a blood alcohol limit of 0.0% effectively prohibits any alcohol consumption before driving. Seatbelt use is mandatory. Road fatalities are high relative to population — Jordan has one of the higher rates in the Middle East. Mobile phone use while driving is prohibited. The Traffic Directorate under the Public Security Directorate enforces traffic law. Point systems and licence suspension have been introduced as additional deterrents.
laws.penalty: Fines, licence suspension, and imprisonment for serious violations; mandatory suspension for drunk driving
exceptions: Military and emergency vehicles exempt from standard traffic regulations
Diplomatic vehicles subject to immunity provisions
Agricultural vehicles in rural areas subject to different standards

quiz.q: What is Jordan's blood alcohol limit for driving?
quiz.explanation: Jordan effectively prohibits any alcohol consumption before driving with a 0.0% blood alcohol limit, reflecting the country's Islamic legal influences.

laws.title: Waqf Administration and Islamic Endowment Law
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for Islamic charitable endowments and property
laws.fullDescription: The Ministry of Awqaf (Islamic Endowments) administers Jordan's waqf system — Islamic charitable endowments that have historically funded mosques, schools, and social services. Waqf properties are inalienable and managed for specified religious or charitable purposes. Jordan's Hashemite monarchy claims custodianship of Islamic and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem, with the king personally overseeing the Waqf administration for the holy city. This custodianship is contested by Palestinian authorities and has been a source of diplomatic tension. Misappropriation of waqf funds is a serious offense.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment and restitution for misappropriation of waqf funds; administrative sanctions for managers
exceptions: Court approval required for any disposal of waqf property
Historical endowments subject to different rules than modern ones
Christian waqf properties managed separately by respective churches

quiz.q: What special custodianship do the Hashemite kings of Jordan claim related to Jerusalem?
options: Custodianship of Islamic and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem
quiz.explanation: Jordan's Hashemite monarchy claims custodianship of Islamic and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem, with the king overseeing the Waqf administration for the holy city.

laws.title: Mental Health Law and Psychiatric Patient Rights
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for mental health treatment and involuntary commitment
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Mental Health Law provides a framework for both voluntary and involuntary psychiatric treatment. Involuntary commitment requires court approval and two medical opinions. Patients have rights to information, humane treatment, and appeal of commitment orders. Mental health services are significantly underfunded relative to need — stigma remains a major barrier to treatment-seeking. UNHCR and international organizations provide mental health support to refugee populations, particularly Syrian refugees dealing with war trauma. The law has been criticized for inadequate protections against indefinite involuntary commitment.
laws.penalty: N/A — regulatory; unauthorized detention of patients without proper commitment procedures subject to criminal liability
exceptions: Emergency psychiatric detention permitted for up to 72 hours before court review
Criminal defendants found mentally unfit tried under different procedures
Children and adolescents subject to separate provisions

quiz.q: What is required for involuntary psychiatric commitment in Jordan?
options: Court approval and two medical opinions
Family consent and one medical opinion
quiz.explanation: Jordan's Mental Health Law requires court approval and two medical opinions for involuntary psychiatric commitment.

laws.title: Decentralization Law No. 49 of 2015 — Governorate Governance
laws.subtitle: Reform devolving some powers to elected provincial councils
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Decentralization Law established elected governorate councils for the first time, shifting some planning and development functions from central government to the 12 governorates. The first governorate council elections were held in 2017. Critics argue the reform was limited — councils lack fiscal authority and most decisions still require central government approval. The law was part of the broader political modernization agenda following Arab Spring pressure. Tribal affiliations heavily influence governorate council elections in rural areas.

quiz.explanation: The first governorate council elections under Jordan's Decentralization Law were held in 2017, marking the first time elected councils existed at the provincial level.

laws.title: Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Law
laws.subtitle: Jordan's framework for combating financial crime
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Law requires financial institutions to implement Know Your Customer procedures, report suspicious transactions, and maintain transaction records. The Anti-Money Laundering Unit (AMLU) coordinates with the Financial Intelligence Unit. Jordan was removed from the FATF grey list in 2023 after implementing required reforms, representing a significant step for the financial sector's international reputation. The law applies to banks, exchange houses, and designated non-financial businesses including real estate agents and lawyers handling financial transactions.
laws.penalty: Fines and imprisonment up to 15 years for money laundering; asset freezing and confiscation

Was added to the FATF blacklist
Was removed from the FATF grey list

laws.title: Urban Planning Law — Zoning and Building Regulations
laws.subtitle: Framework for urban development, zoning, and construction permits
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's urban planning is governed by the Greater Amman Municipality Law, regional planning bodies, and the Urban Planning and Environment Law. Building permits are required for all construction; unauthorized structures are subject to demolition orders — a major issue given population growth from refugee influx. Zoning regulations designate residential, commercial, and industrial areas. Rapid urbanization driven by refugee arrivals has strained infrastructure in cities like Irbid near the Syrian border. Building codes incorporate seismic considerations given Jordan's location in the Jordan Rift Valley earthquake zone.
laws.penalty: Demolition orders for unauthorized construction; fines; revocation of building permits
exceptions: Emergency shelters for displaced populations may receive temporary exemption
Agricultural structures in rural areas subject to different rules
Heritage zones have additional restrictions preventing demolition of historic structures

quiz.q: Why have urban planning pressures intensified in Jordanian cities like Irbid?
quiz.explanation: Rapid urbanization driven by refugee influx — particularly Syrian refugees — has strained infrastructure in Jordanian cities near the Syrian border like Irbid.

laws.title: Consumer Protection Law No. 7 of 2017
laws.subtitle: Governs consumer rights, product liability, and market practices
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Consumer Protection Law establishes rights including truthful product information, safety standards, and redress mechanisms. The Consumer Protection Directorate under the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply investigates complaints and can issue fines for misleading advertising or unsafe products. Price gouging during shortages is addressed through the law and the Price Monitoring Directorate. During the COVID-19 pandemic, consumer protection enforcement was enhanced to prevent excessive pricing of medical supplies. The law also addresses online consumer transactions.
laws.penalty: Fines of JD 100–50,000 for violations; product recall orders; business licence suspension
exceptions: Agricultural raw products exempt from some labeling requirements
Custom-made goods not subject to standard consumer goods provisions

quiz.q: Which body investigates consumer protection complaints in Jordan?
quiz.explanation: The Consumer Protection Directorate under Jordan's Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply investigates consumer complaints and enforces consumer rights.

laws.title: State Security Court — Jurisdiction and Procedure
laws.subtitle: Jordan's specialized court for national security and terrorism cases
laws.fullDescription: The State Security Court (SSC) was established to handle cases involving national security, terrorism, drug trafficking, and certain other serious offenses. It operates under a distinct procedure from ordinary courts with limited appeal rights. Military judges participate in SSC panels alongside civilian judges. Human rights organizations have documented due process concerns including limited access to counsel, prolonged pre-trial detention, and reliance on confessions. The SSC has been used to prosecute journalists, activists, and Islamist politicians in addition to genuine security cases.

quiz.explanation: Military judges participate alongside civilian judges in Jordan's State Security Court panels, contributing to concerns about full independence from executive influence.

laws.title: Aviation Law and JCAR Regulations
laws.subtitle: Civil aviation law and Jordan's aviation regulatory framework
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's civil aviation is governed by the Civil Aviation Regulatory Commission (CARC) under the Civil Aviation Law. Royal Jordanian is the national carrier. Jordan serves as a regional aviation hub, with Queen Alia International Airport handling significant international traffic. The airport and aviation sector are important to Jordan's tourism and business travel economy. Aviation safety standards are aligned with ICAO requirements. Jordan has bilateral air service agreements with numerous countries. Low-cost carrier services have expanded regional connectivity.
laws.penalty: Fines and grounding of aircraft for safety violations; criminal prosecution for aviation offenses

Diplomatic aircraft subject to international aviation conventions

quiz.explanation: Royal Jordanian is Jordan's national airline carrier, operating from Queen Alia International Airport which serves as a regional aviation hub.

laws.title: Nature Reserve and Protected Areas Law
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for Jordan's biodiversity conservation
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature (RSCN) manages a network of nature reserves covering significant biodiversity. The Dana Biosphere Reserve, Wadi Rum Protected Area, and Azraq Wetland Reserve are key conservation areas. Hunting of protected species is prohibited. The Protected Areas Law establishes buffer zones around reserves where development is restricted. Ecotourism has been developed as a sustainable income source for communities adjacent to reserves. International designations including UNESCO biosphere reserve status enhance legal protections.

laws.title: Non-Governmental Organizations Law No. 51 of 2008
laws.subtitle: Governs registration, activities, and oversight of civil society
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's NGO Law regulates the registration and operation of non-governmental organizations. All NGOs must register with the Ministry of Social Development and obtain approval for foreign funding. A 2022 amendment tightened provisions around foreign funding transparency. The law has been used to restrict organizations working on political reform, LGBTQ+ rights, and criticism of government policy. International human rights organizations have documented cases of NGO deregistration and harassment. Jordan hosts a significant number of international organizations given its stability relative to regional neighbors.

quiz.explanation: Jordan's NGOs must register with the Ministry of Social Development, which also approves foreign funding under the 2008 NGO Law.

laws.title: Medical Malpractice and Healthcare Standards
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for medical liability and patient rights
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's healthcare liability framework covers medical malpractice through both civil tort law and professional disciplinary systems. The Jordan Medical Association self-regulates the medical profession with disciplinary boards for complaints. Civil suits for malpractice are possible but challenging — Jordan lacks dedicated medical malpractice legislation. Criminal prosecution for gross negligence is theoretically possible. Patient rights to informed consent and medical records are recognized in policy but inconsistently enforced. Jordan's healthcare workforce is a major export — significant numbers of Jordanian doctors and nurses work in Gulf states.

laws.title: Public Security Law — Police Powers and Accountability
laws.subtitle: Legal framework governing Jordan's police force
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Public Security Directorate (PSD) operates under the Public Security Law and falls under the Ministry of Interior. The PSD has authority to detain individuals for investigation for up to 48 hours without charge, renewable by prosecutors. The Internal Security Force (Darak) handles riot control. Complaints against police are handled internally with limited independent oversight. Human rights organizations have documented cases of excessive force and torture in detention. Political events — particularly protests related to economic grievances or regional conflicts — have led to significant clampdowns.

quiz.explanation: Jordan's Public Security Law allows police to detain individuals for up to 48 hours without charge, renewable by prosecutors.

laws.title: E-Government and Digital Services Framework
laws.subtitle: Jordan's digital government infrastructure and service delivery
laws.fullDescription: Jordan has been a regional leader in e-government development through the Reach initiative and Jordan Vision 2025. The Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship oversees digital transformation. Key platforms include MyGov.jo for unified government services, digital ID systems, and electronic court filings. The National Information Technology Center provides infrastructure. Jordan's tech sector — including the Aqaba Technology Village and various incubators — has benefited from the e-government framework. Data privacy concerns have been raised as digital services expand.

quiz.explanation: MyGov.jo is Jordan's unified government digital services platform, part of the country's regional leadership in e-government development.

laws.title: Zakat and Social Welfare System
laws.subtitle: Islamic charitable giving system and government social safety nets
laws.fullDescription: Jordan operates a dual social welfare system combining government programs and Islamic charitable institutions. The National Aid Fund provides cash transfers to poor families. Zakat (Islamic obligatory almsgiving) is collected and distributed through the Ministry of Awqaf. Jordan's social protection system has been strained by refugee arrivals and economic shocks. The 2021 National Social Protection Strategy aimed to consolidate and improve coverage. International donors including the World Bank and EU support social protection programs. quiz.explanation: Jordan's Ministry of Awqaf collects and distributes Zakat (Islamic obligatory almsgiving) as part of the country's dual social welfare system.

laws.title: Royal Prerogatives — King's Constitutional Powers
laws.subtitle: Extensive executive, legislative, and judicial powers of the Hashemite monarch
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's 1952 Constitution, as amended, grants the king broad executive powers: he appoints the prime minister and can dismiss the government, dissolves parliament (which has occurred numerous times), issues Royal Decrees with legal force when parliament is dissolved, and serves as Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces. The king appoints all senators, the President of the Constitutional Court, and senior judiciary. In practice, all major policy decisions require royal approval. laws.title: Aqaba Port and Maritime Law
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for Jordan's only sea port
laws.fullDescription: Jordan has only 26 kilometers of coastline on the Red Sea at Aqaba — its sole outlet to international maritime trade. The Aqaba Container Terminal is operated under a concession arrangement and is critical to Jordanian import/export logistics. Maritime law applies UNCLOS frameworks and local port regulations. The ASEZA (Aqaba Special Economic Zone Authority) governs port-adjacent commercial activities. Jordan has invested heavily in port infrastructure to handle the Aqaba corridor, which serves as a supply route to Iraq and Saudi Arabia.

laws.title: Jordan National Census and Civil Registration
laws.subtitle: Population registration, civil status, and national identity systems
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Department of Civil Status and Passports maintains the national population register. All residents must register; birth, marriage, divorce, and death registration are mandatory. The national ID number (Raqm Watani) is required for virtually all government and many private services. Palestinian refugees with Jordanian citizenship are registered as full citizens; West Bank holders of Jordanian passports have limited status. Syrian refugees may register with civil authorities but face different status. The census provides planning data for services though accurate refugee counting remains challenging.

quiz.explanation: Jordan's national ID number (Raqm Watani) is required for virtually all government and many private services, maintained by the Department of Civil Status and Passports.

laws.title: Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Law No. 13 of 2012
laws.subtitle: Framework driving Jordan's solar and wind energy transition
laws.fullDescription: Jordan imports over 90% of its energy needs, making the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Law critical to energy security and economic sustainability. The law enabled private power purchase agreements for solar and wind projects. Jordan has become a regional leader in renewable energy — the Ma'an Development Area hosts major solar facilities. The Masdar solar project and multiple wind farms have significantly expanded clean energy capacity. Jordan's target of 50% renewable energy by 2030 drives ongoing investment. quiz.explanation: Jordan targets 50% renewable energy by 2030, driven by its Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Law and the critical need to reduce reliance on imported energy.

laws.title: Penal Code — Crimes Against Public Order

These provisions interact with the Public Gatherings Law (requiring prior notice for demonstrations) to create a broad legal framework for restricting public protest. Participation in unlawful assemblies can result in imprisonment even without personal acts of violence. Following the Arab Spring, these provisions were used alongside anti-terrorism laws to prosecute protest organizers. Security forces dispersing protests have used these provisions to justify detention of demonstrators.

laws.title: Vocational Training and Technical Education Law
laws.subtitle: Framework for Jordan's technical workforce development
laws.fullDescription: The Vocational Training Corporation (VTC) operates Jordan's technical and vocational education system. Given youth unemployment exceeding 40% in some metrics and a skills mismatch in the labor market, vocational training is a policy priority. The law mandates coordination between training programs and employer needs. Partnerships with German, Japanese, and other international technical training institutions have been developed. Syrian and other refugees participate in some vocational training programs as part of the Jordan Compact framework linking humanitarian support to development outcomes.
laws.penalty: N/A — educational framework
exceptions: Private vocational institutes operate under separate accreditation
Foreign certifications recognized through bilateral agreements
Aqaba SEZ has sector-specific training programs

quiz.explanation: Youth unemployment exceeding 40% in some metrics and labor market skills mismatch make vocational training a major policy priority in Jordan.

laws.title: Defamation Law — Criminal and Civil Provisions
laws.subtitle: Jordan's broad defamation laws and their use against critics
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Penal Code criminalizes defamation and libel, with enhanced penalties for defaming public officials. The Press and Publications Law adds additional provisions for media defamation. Unlike many Western jurisdictions, the burden of proof in criminal defamation cases is on the defendant to prove truth as a defense. The laws have been extensively used against journalists, bloggers, and opposition figures critical of government policies. International human rights bodies have called for decriminalization of defamation. The Cybercrime Law 2023 extended defamation provisions to online speech.
laws.penalty: 3 months–2 years imprisonment; fines; enhanced penalties for defaming public officials
exceptions: Parliamentary immunity protects MPs for statements made in parliament
Academic and peer-reviewed publications may have more latitude
Public interest journalism defense exists but is difficult to apply successfully

quiz.q: What is notable about the burden of proof in Jordan's criminal defamation cases?
options: The state must prove intent to harm
The defendant must prove truth as a defense
quiz.explanation: In Jordan's criminal defamation cases, the burden is on the defendant to prove truth as a defense — unlike many Western systems where the prosecution must prove falsity.

laws.title: Public Procurement Law — Government Contracting
laws.subtitle: Rules governing how Jordan's government awards contracts
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Public Procurement Law requires competitive tendering for government contracts above threshold amounts. The General Supplies Directorate oversees procurement for central government. Municipalities have their own procurement processes subject to oversight from the Ministry of Municipal Affairs. International competitive bidding is required for large infrastructure contracts, often funded by World Bank or other international loans. Corruption in procurement has been a documented concern — several high-profile cases involved inflated contracts for military supplies and infrastructure projects.
laws.penalty: Fines, imprisonment, and permanent disqualification for procurement fraud; contract cancellation
exceptions: Emergency procurement can bypass normal tender requirements
Defense procurement has classified procedures
Direct procurement from sole-source suppliers permitted in specific technical circumstances

quiz.q: What type of bidding is required for large infrastructure contracts in Jordan?
quiz.explanation: Jordan requires international competitive bidding for large infrastructure contracts, particularly those funded by World Bank or other international financing.

laws.title: Human Trafficking Law No. 9 of 2009
laws.subtitle: Jordan's anti-trafficking framework and victim protections
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Anti-Human Trafficking Law criminalizes trafficking in persons for labor and sexual exploitation. Penalties are severe, with trafficking of children carrying enhanced sentences. The National Committee for Combating Human Trafficking coordinates inter-agency response. Jordan has been criticized in US State Department Tier 2 Watch List reports for insufficient prosecution of trafficking cases and inadequate protection for victims — particularly domestic workers who are identified as trafficking victims and then deported. The tourism and domestic work sectors have seen documented trafficking cases.
laws.penalty: 5–10 years imprisonment for trafficking; 10–15 years for trafficking children or organized crime involvement

Foreign victim witnesses may receive temporary residency to testify
Children have enhanced protections and are placed in specialized facilities

laws.title: Privacy Law — Physical Search and Surveillance
laws.subtitle: Legal requirements for search warrants and surveillance authorization
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Code of Criminal Procedure requires judicial warrants for search of private premises. However, the Anti-Terrorism Law and powers granted to the GID provide significant surveillance authority with limited judicial oversight. Wiretapping requires authorization under the Telecommunications Law but intelligence services operate with broader powers. The Cybercrime Law 2023 grants authorities access to communications data from service providers with limited procedural requirements. International technical surveillance assistance has expanded Jordan's monitoring capabilities through cooperation with US and European intelligence agencies.
laws.penalty: Evidence obtained without proper warrant may be inadmissible; officials conducting illegal searches face disciplinary action
exceptions: Exigent circumstances allow warrantless search in some situations
Anti-terrorism cases subject to different procedural rules
Intelligence operations not required to follow same evidentiary rules as criminal prosecution

Authorities' access to communications data from service providers

laws.title: Maternity Leave and Working Mothers' Rights
laws.subtitle: Legal protections for pregnant workers and nursing mothers
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Labour Law provides 10 weeks of fully paid maternity leave for female employees, which may be extended by unpaid leave. Employers with 20 or more employees must provide nursing breaks and, if 10 or more female employees work in one location, a childcare facility or allowance. Dismissal of a pregnant employee or one on maternity leave is prohibited. The law also provides for paternity leave — fathers are entitled to 3 days of leave. Despite these provisions, women's labor force participation in Jordan remains among the lowest globally, at approximately 14%.
laws.penalty: Fines for employers violating maternity provisions; reinstatement orders for wrongful dismissal
exceptions: Domestic workers excluded from Labour Law maternity provisions

quiz.explanation: Jordan's Labour Law provides 10 weeks of fully paid maternity leave for female employees, with additional unpaid leave possible.

laws.title: Nationality Law — Gender Discrimination in Citizenship Transmission
laws.subtitle: Jordan's restrictive nationality law for children of Jordanian mothers
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Nationality Law of 1954 (as amended) follows patrilineal citizenship — children acquire citizenship through their father, not their mother. Jordanian women married to non-Jordanian men (often Palestinians) cannot pass citizenship to their children. This affects an estimated 80,000 children who are Jordanian by culture but non-citizen by law. These children face barriers to education, healthcare, and employment. Reform campaigns have been ongoing for decades but successive governments have resisted change, citing fears of Palestinian naturalization implications for Jordan's demographic composition and the Israeli-Palestinian peace process.
laws.penalty: N/A — structural legal discrimination rather than a penalty-based provision
exceptions: Children of Jordanian fathers automatically receive citizenship
Stateless children may petition for facilitated naturalization
Presidential (royal) discretion allows individual cases to be resolved
