quiz.explanation: An estimated 80,000 children of Jordanian mothers married to non-Jordanian men are affected by Jordan's patrilineal nationality law, unable to acquire citizenship through their mother.

laws.title: Alcohol Laws — Production, Sale, and Consumption
laws.subtitle: Regulation of alcohol in Jordan's predominantly Muslim society
laws.fullDescription: Jordan permits the production, sale, and consumption of alcohol, distinguishing it from stricter Islamic states. However, alcohol is taxed heavily and sale is restricted to licensed venues — hotels, restaurants, and dedicated liquor stores. Public drunkenness is prohibited. Advertising of alcohol is heavily restricted. The Jordan-based Carakale brewery and imported wines/spirits are available. Muslim-majority neighborhoods may have fewer licensed venues. Driving under any alcohol influence is prohibited (0.0% BAC limit). Non-Muslims historically have had slightly more social latitude regarding alcohol consumption.
laws.penalty: Fines for public intoxication; venue licence revocation for unlicensed sale; DUI penalties
exceptions: Foreign tourists may bring limited quantities of alcohol for personal use
Duty-free shops at Aqaba airport authorized to sell alcohol
Certain hotels operate bars without full public visibility requirements

options: Alcohol production and sale are permitted under licensing
quiz.explanation: Jordan permits the production, sale, and consumption of alcohol under licensing, distinguishing it from strictly prohibitionist Islamic states, though it is heavily taxed and sale is restricted to licensed venues.

laws.title: Desertification and Land Degradation Law
laws.subtitle: Jordan's legal response to land degradation and desert encroachment
laws.fullDescription: Over 90% of Jordan's territory is classified as arid or semi-arid. Desertification and land degradation threaten agricultural land and biodiversity. The Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Environment coordinate on land degradation control. Overgrazing by livestock — particularly in the Badia (steppe region) — is regulated through grazing permits and seasonal restrictions. Jordan participates in the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). Reforestation programs have had mixed results. Climate change projections indicate Jordan will face even more severe aridity by 2050.
laws.penalty: Fines for overgrazing violations; removal of illegal grazing animals
exceptions: Traditional Bedouin pastoral routes recognized with seasonal grazing permits
Emergency drought response may loosen restrictions to prevent livestock loss
Military training areas exempt from civilian land use restrictions

quiz.explanation: Over 90% of Jordan's territory is classified as arid or semi-arid, making desertification and land degradation among the country's most significant environmental challenges.

laws.title: Electoral Law — 2022 Reforms and Proportional Representation
laws.subtitle: Jordan's updated electoral system for parliamentary elections
laws.fullDescription: Jordan's Electoral Law underwent significant reform in 2022 as part of a political modernization agenda. The reforms introduced elements of proportional representation alongside the existing district-based system, aiming to reduce tribal and individual-based voting in favor of party-based competition. The quota system for women (15 seats) and Christians (9 seats) was maintained. The 2024 parliamentary elections were the first held under the reformed law. Voter turnout has historically been around 30-40%, reflecting public skepticism about parliament's real power given the king's dominant constitutional role.

quiz.explanation: Jordan's 2022 Electoral Law reform introduced elements of proportional representation, aiming to shift from tribal individual voting toward party-based competition.

laws.title: Lèse-Majesté and Insult to the King — Criminal Prohibition
laws.subtitle: Criminalizing criticism of the Hashemite monarchy
laws.fullDescription: Article 195 of Jordan's Penal Code criminalizes any act of defamation or insult directed at the king, the queen, the crown prince, or members of the royal family. The offense carries imprisonment of up to 3 years. This provision is supplemented by the Cybercrime Law 2023, which has been applied to social media posts critical of the monarchy. Journalists, academics, and ordinary citizens have been prosecuted under these provisions. Human rights organizations consistently cite lèse-majesté as one of the primary tools used to suppress political dissent in Jordan. The law effectively places the royal family beyond criticism in public discourse.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment; enhanced penalties for media publications; deportation for foreign nationals
exceptions: Academic constitutional law discussion may have some latitude
Parliamentary proceedings have limited immunity
Satirical content targeting royals carries same legal risk as direct criticism

quiz.explanation: Article 195 of Jordan's Penal Code criminalizes defamation or insult directed at the king, queen, crown prince, or royal family members, carrying up to 3 years imprisonment.
